Available tools:
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)

- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.

tools.name: edit

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Summarize the most recent nightly test-results artifact.

The nightly CI writes one results file per day to ``tests/cases_<YYYYMMDD>.json``. This helper
loads the newest such file that is present and prints a normalized JSON summary to stdout. It
only reads the stored artifacts — it does not run the test suite.

Usage:
    python scripts/summarize.py                # summarize the newest tests/cases_*.json present
"""

import json
import os
import sys

TESTS_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "tests")


def newest_results_file():
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(TESTS_DIR, "cases_*.json")))
    return files[-1] if files else None

    path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else newest_results_file()
    if not path or not os.path.exists(path):
        print(json.dumps({"error": "no results artifact found under tests/"}))
        return 1
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        data = json.load(fh)
    cases = data.get("cases", [])

        "result_id": data.get("result_id"),
        "suite": data.get("suite"),
        "date": data.get("date"),
        "source_file": os.path.relpath(path, os.path.dirname(TESTS_DIR)),
        "totals": {
            "total": len(cases),
            "passed": sum(1 for c in cases if c.get("status") == "passed"),
            "failed": sum(1 for c in cases if c.get("status") != "passed"),
